title: Solicitation, tobacco, attendance and sexual-harassment policies - 2025 handbook
summary: 2025 handbook rules on workplace solicitation/distribution, tobacco use, no-fault attendance/point discipline and sexual harassment reporting/discipline.

claims.claim: Employees may not distribute literature, sell merchandise, solicit contributions, or solicit for causes in the workplace during working time or through RTEC email/telephonic systems without management approval; non-staff solicitation/distribution on RTEC property is prohibited.
Smoking and tobacco use are prohibited inside RTEC facilities and in RTEC-owned and leased vehicles.
RTEC describes a no-fault attendance policy requiring employees to be present, on time, at the workstation ready at shift start, and remain through shift end.

Excused absences include policy-provided leave, illness under stated documentation rules, prior supervisor approval, or supervisor-recognized emergencies; unexcused absences and no-call/no-show conduct can result in termination under the handbook.

The attendance policy assigns points by duration: 4 hours or less = 1/4 point, 4-6 hours = 1/2 point, 7 hours or more = 1 point; it states verbal warning at the stated initial threshold, written warning at 2 points, three-day unpaid suspension at 4 points, and termination at 6 points.

evidence.note: The source formatting around the first verbal-warning threshold is imperfect; full source text is preserved for review.

claims.claim: Employees who will be absent must call at least two hours before the department or employee start time, whichever comes first, and must call each day absent unless otherwise instructed; failure to call results in disciplinary action.
Funeral leave, jury duty, FMLA leave with proper documentation, and workers' compensation incidents are stated not to generate attendance points.

RTEC states sexual harassment is unacceptable and includes both quid-pro-quo-type conduct and conduct that creates an intimidating, hostile or offensive work environment; harassing conduct is subject to discipline.

claims.claim: Employees who experience sexual harassment are encouraged to report/discuss it with their supervisor, Human Resource Manager, or Executive Director.

trigger: Solicitation/distribution activity, tobacco use, employee absence/tardiness, or harassment concern.
systems: RTEC email and telephonic communication systems
steps: Classify absence as excused/unexcused and determine point treatment.
Record attendance points and apply stated progressive consequences.
Require daily absence notification unless otherwise instructed.
Route harassment reports to supervisor, HR Manager, or Executive Director.
decisions: Whether conduct violates harassment or solicitation policy
deadlines: Absence call-in at least two hours before applicable start time.
Daily call-in for each day absent unless instructed otherwise.
exceptions: Documented FMLA, workers' compensation, jury duty and funeral leave are excluded from attendance points as stated.
Management approval can authorize certain solicitation/distribution activity.
unresolved_questions: Clarify the formatting/threshold for the verbal-warning line in the attendance point schedule.
Identify the current harassment complaint form/investigation procedure that operationalizes the handbook reporting statement.
automation_candidates: Attendance point calculator with protected-leave exclusions and human review.
Harassment intake routing with restricted access.
